newsitem.title: UK: P&O hit by Eurotunnel agreement with banks.
newsitem.headline: P&O hit by Eurotunnel agreement with banks.

text.p: Shares in Britain's Peninsular and Oriental Steam Navigation Co came under pressure on Thursday morning after cross-channel rival Eurotunnel announced an agreement with its banks, dealers said.
P&O shares were down 6.5 pence, or 1.06 percent, to 605p by 0900 GMT, while the FTSE-100 index was 8.6 points, or 0.20 percent, higher at 4,396.3.
Anglo-French Channel Tunnel operator Eurotunnel Plc /SA said in a statement that a steering committee of banks had agreed a restructuring of its eight billion stg debt.
The plan will ensure the financial stability of the company for the next six years, Eurotunnel said.
Separately, P&O said on Thursday it had placed an order at the Meyer Werft shipyard in Germany for a 76,000 ton cruise ship that would cost 200 million stg.
The ship, to be delivered for service in the spring of 2000, will carry more than 1,800 passengers on a wide range of global cruises from Britain.
